title: 10. Exercises: Day 16 — Human-in-the-Loop

objectives: Solve the Day 16 — Human-in-the-Loop exercises without looking at the lesson
Test edge cases and explain your approach

sections.title: Exercises
sections.body:
1. **Persist across process restarts.** Replace `MemorySaver` with `SqliteSaver` (from `langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite`). Verify that you can start the workflow, kill the process, restart, and resume from the same `thread_id`.

<details>
<summary>Hint</summary>

`from langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite import SqliteSaver; import sqlite3; conn = sqlite3.connect("checkpoints.db", check_same_thread=False); checkpointer = SqliteSaver(conn)`. Then use it like MemorySaver. To test restart-resume, run the script, answer one prompt, Ctrl-C, then run again with the same thread_id and the same initial call (or skip the initial call and go straight to the resume loop).
</details>

2. **Add a "edit inline" option.** Instead of giving feedback and letting the agent revise, let the human paste a full replacement draft. The workflow should accept it, validate it fits the schema, and skip refinement.

<details>
<summary>Hint</summary>

Add a third action `"inline"`. Read the body from `input()` (multiline: read until empty line). Construct a `Draft` directly with `Draft(title=old.title, body=new_body, word_count=len(new_body.split()))`. Skip the refiner call and present the new draft for approval.
</details>

3. **Time-out the human.** If the human does not respond within 60 seconds, auto-approve and send. (Hint: use `signal.alarm` on Unix or `threading.Timer`.)

<details>
<summary>Hint</summary>

Use `signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, handler); signal.alarm(60)` before `input()`. In the handler, raise a `TimeoutError` and catch it in the workflow, treating it as approve. Reset the alarm with `signal.alarm(0)` after each input. On Windows, use `threading.Timer(60, lambda: ...)` instead.
</details>
